newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan investment in China down 27 pct in Jan-Feb.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan investment in China down 27 pct in Jan-Feb.

text.p: Taiwan's indirect investment in China fell an annual 27 percent in January-February to $104.7 million following the government's call to slow investment there, the Investment Commission said on Tuesday.
The commission said it had approved 39 investment projects in the rival communist mainland in the two-month period.
The commission attributed the fall in part to its having postponed an investment screening meeting to early March from February.

Investments focused mainly on Jiangsu, Guangdong, Shandong, Zhejiang and Hebei provinces, with major investments in electronics and electrical appliances, plastics, chemicals manufacturing, retail and basic metals industries, it said.
Taiwan has banned direct investment and trade with China since a civil war split them in 1949.

Since a political thaw began in the late 1980s, some 30,000 Taiwan firms have poured over US$30 billion into the mainland, making Taiwan one of China's top overseas investors and China one of Taiwan's most important markets.

Increased political and even military tensions in the past two years have prompted Taiwan's Nationalist government to call for more caution in mainland investing, warning that the island must not become overdependent on its adversary's economy.
Several major Taiwan firms have called off China projects in apparent compliance.
